newsitem.title: USA: Interwest Medical revs rise, net falls.
newsitem.headline: Interwest Medical revs rise, net falls.

text.p: Interwest Home Medical Inc said total revenues for the three month periods ended Dec. 31, 1996 and 1995 were $5,382,160 compared to $4,565,675, an increase of about 18 percent.

"Our record revenues are due primarily to continued double-digit revenue growth from our continuing stores and to geographic growth as a result of the businesses acquired by Interwest during 1996," stated James E. Robinson, president and chief executive officer for Interwest Home Medical Inc.

For the three month period ended Dec. 31, 1996, the company had net income of $110,273 compared to $153,978 for the three month period ended Dec. 31, 1995. The decrease is primarily due to acquisition costs, losses from home elevator operations which were sold in December of 1996, two start-up branches established in the final four months of the fiscal year and increased interest expense due to borrowings to fund acquisitions.

Earnings per share for the three month periods ended Dec. 31, 1996 and 1995 were 3 cents and 5 cents on 3.3 million average shares outstanding for both periods. Acquisition of Indian Valley Medical Services
